title: He Rejected My $18 Receipt. The Auditor Found $4,800.
script: My manager rejected an $18 client-lunch reimbursement because the receipt was slightly faded. He announced that every expense needed perfect documentation, no exceptions. Fine. I resubmitted mine with the restaurant's duplicate receipt, a bank statement, the meeting invite, and the client's thank-you email. Then accounting asked me to help reconcile our team's overdue expense file. I applied his rule exactly. His corporate card had $4,800 in charges labeled business development with no receipts, attendees, or notes. Mostly steakhouse tabs and weekend rides. I flagged every line instead of guessing. The controller froze his card and scheduled an audit. He told me I should have used common sense because everyone knew his expenses were legitimate. I forwarded his no-exceptions email. My $18 lunch was approved that afternoon. His expenses took six weeks, three interviews, and one newly mandatory receipt-scanning app. The faded receipt survived.
